subject: Consolidated-tier proposal for Exhibit B (pricing thresholds)
messages:
From: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@olivesys.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@olivesys.com, pricing@olivesys.com
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: consolidate thresholds across Exhibit B

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. The procurement team reviewed Exhibit B and would like to propose consolidating the three SKU-specific threshold bands into a single consolidated tier for billing and true-up. The idea: simplify our forecast model and eliminate per-SKU guardrails that cause monthly jaggedness.

Attached is a redline from our side (Olive_ExhibitB_ConsolidatedProposal.pdf) that: 1) combines SKU thresholds into a single annualized minimum, 2) replaces per-SKU floors with a blended floor, and 3) proposes a 6-month grace window for any volume true-ups.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood accept consolidated thresholds with a blended floor?
- Would you agree to a reduced penalty rate (from 120% to 110%) during year-one adoption?
- We expect to finalize the Order Form once legal confirms language.

If helpful, happy to set a 30-minute call tomorrow for walk-through.

Best,
Jamie Torres
Senior Procurement Manager — Olive Systems
jamie.torres@olivesys.com
Attachment: Olive_ExhibitB_ConsolidatedProposal.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@olivesys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: consolidate thresholds across Exhibit B

Jamie —

Thanks for the clean proposal and the PDF; this is a helpful starting point. I reviewed the consolidated-tier approach with sales and finance. We like the simplicity for invoicing, but two items need clarification from legal before we can accept the blended floor and the 6-month grace on true-ups:

1) Downside protection: our standard pricing guardrail includes a minimum per-SKU floor to avoid cross-subsidization across product lines. Combining into a blended floor is acceptable if we include a clause that prevents retroactive reallocation that drives below-cost consumption for a single SKU. We proposed language in the attached Redwood_ExhibitB_Markup_v2.pdf (see Section 2.1 comment).

2) Penalty rate: we can move on your suggestion to 110% in year one conditional on a one-time adoption credit to offset initial forecasting friction. Proposed credit: a one-month credit equal to 8% of the first quarter invoice. We put the suggested credit calculation in the markup.

I’m looping in Marissa (legal) and Ben (pricing) for redline review and to confirm the operational mechanics for true-ups (monthly vs. quarterly). If we can align on the anti-cross-subsidization clause and detail the credit calculation, I believe we can get this into an Order Form cleanly.

I’ve attached our markup and a diff XLS that highlights how billing would move across lines.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
Attachments: Redwood_ExhibitB_Markup_v2.pdf (PDF, 58KB); OrderForm_Annex_Diff.xlsx (XLSX, 23KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: consolidate thresholds across Exhibit B — legal notes

Markus / Ben —

Thanks for the loop. I reviewed both PDFs and pulled out the legal-risk items for negotiation. Two comments from a legal perspective (keeps it tight while still being partner-friendly):

- Anti-cross-subsidization carve (Markus referenced): propose this language: "The consolidated floor shall not be applied to reallocate historical usage in a manner that reduces the effective per-SKU price below Redwood’s published minimums for that SKU for any prior billing period." This prevents retroactive crediting that would create unexpected exposure.

- Grace window: a 6-month grace for true-ups is reasonable, but we need to be explicit about timing and the measurement period (calendar month vs. billing month). Recommend quarterly true-ups with monthly reporting; true-up payments to be settled within 45 days of quarter close.

Operational note for Ben: if we accept blended floor with quarterly true-ups, can pricing ops compute the blended floor deterministically each quarter and expose the computation in the invoice line item? That transparency will reduce queries.

If Ben signs off, I’m comfortable presenting this redline to Olive with the proposed adoption credit mechanics included.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@olivesys.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@olivesys.com, pricing@olivesys.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: consolidate thresholds across Exhibit B

Markus / Marissa / Ben —

Appreciate the quick review and the clear next steps. Olive is willing to accept the anti-cross-subsidization clause as drafted by Marissa — that language makes sense for our finance team as well. We’re also OK moving to quarterly true-ups with monthly reporting, settled within 45 days.

On the adoption credit: Olive would prefer a fixed credit approach instead of a percent-of-quarter calculation to simplify onboarding accounting. Proposed: a one-time $25,000 adoption credit applied to the first invoice after execution. Would Redwood accept that in place of the 8%-of-Q1 calculation?

If yes, we’ll update the attached PDF and re-submit for final legal redline.

Also attaching a clean ExhibitB with the single-tier numbers filled in (Olive_ExhibitB_ConsolidatedProposal_FINAL.pdf).

Can we target signature (DocuSign) by 3/26? I can coordinate with our legal if you confirm the final credit approach.

Thanks —
Jamie Torres
Senior Procurement Manager — Olive Systems
jamie.torres@olivesys.com
